summary: Retrained from the previous best single neural policy for the wider workspace and higher acceleration. The selected candidate retains learned shot selection, improves requested fast-shot success in the expanded simulation, and improves difficult corner recovery. Its remaining thermal and possession weaknesses are shown below.
changes: Expanded the simulated paddle-center workspace to give 30 mm rim clearance at the side and back rails. The forward boundary is 1200 mm in the physical grid frame.
Raised the simulated acceleration cap from 60 to 100 m/s²; retained the 12 m/s speed ceiling.
Added a mild position-based dwell cost near the rails. Edge visits are allowed; lingering accumulates a cost.
Refitted per-motor current and thermal dynamics from the post-replacement logs, retaining each drive’s measured RMS settings.
Practiced unpredictable fast releases and trained on successful neural corner-recovery attempts. Every runtime action still comes from one neural network.
training_method: The actor started from possession-20260926-v3, with a training-only coordinate conversion for the larger action workspace. PPO continued on self-play, possession and defense exercises. The final corner-recovery pass imitated successful noisy rollouts from that learned actor while preserving its ordinary skills; no scripted recovery controller or scripted action labels were used.
comparison_method: Previous policy and candidate were tested on matched seeded fixtures in the same expanded simulation and updated motor model, including simulated sensing delay. The old policy’s actions were converted to preserve their original physical targets and acceleration requests, except for the new decoder’s 5 m/s² minimum effort floor. Core shooting and defense use larger held-out cohorts; the corner rows are development diagnostics. These are simulated results, not measurements against a human.
comparison_rows: Requested fast shots: receiving at 3–8 m/s
Slow outgoing puck: control then requested fast shot
reward_rows: Retain straight, left-bank and right-bank conditioning
Control the puck and turn possession into a shot
Reduce uncovered goal width before a fast release
Quadratic cost inside the outer 6 cm of the allowed center workspace; no extra exclusion zone
Penalize motor energy, hot load state and modeled shutdown
endurance_rows: Fresh confirmation: 8 × 10 minutes; initial load 50%, gain 1.0
load_conclusion: The selected candidate passed the 16-match nominal cohort with a 94.3% peak and a fresh eight-match confirmation with a 92.0% peak. It failed 5 of 16 hot-start stress matches, peaking at 107.5%. It is a simulation candidate, not an RMS-safe physical release. The outer load map is extrapolated and still needs measurements.
limitations: Hot-start sustained load failures remain: 5/16 matches crossed the modeled threshold. The independent nominal cohort passed, but that does not establish universal safety.
The expanded physical travel area has not been probed in this session. No robot, camera or motors were activated.
The live runner still uses the previous workspace. This package is simulation-only and is rejected by the legacy physical adapter until workspace integration and physical qualification are completed.
Fast human shots can be impossible to reach after release; anticipatory positioning matters. These tests do not establish superhuman defense.
Difficult corner recovery remains inconsistent, and long rallies can still stall. Slow outgoing possession is reported separately so regressions are visible.
Rail contact projection fixes a simulation overlap artifact, but real paddle tilt, bounce, cable slack and corner holding currents still need measurements.
The 14–16 m/s subset did not improve over the previous policy (244 vs 245 saves in 342 trials). The aggregate defense gain comes from slower shots in the 10–16 m/s range.
selection_method: Checkpoint selection considered requested fast shots, moving-release saves, corner recovery, long-match thermal behavior and motion-cap audits. The latest training checkpoint was not automatically preferred. A fresh eight-match nominal cohort was evaluated after shortlisting; no further fitting used those fixtures.
experiment_findings: The balanced PPO branch produced the strongest shooting results, but failed some long nominal and hot-load matches.
Longer coherent neural exploration and successful-trajectory imitation improved corner recovery without adding a tactical controller.
Stronger edge penalties, thermal urgency, forecast holding-load penalties and policy averaging were tested separately; their development and independent failures remain in the logs.

The final fast-release defense continuation practiced 10–18 m/s shots with stronger pre-release coverage rewards. Its final development save count was 295/384 versus 294/384 for the selected candidate, corner recovery fell to 12/128 versus 22/128, and all four snapshots failed the hot-load screen; it was not selected.

provenance.replay_description: Full unedited first match of a four-match fixed-seed self-play audit; both sides use the selected checkpoint.
